stem.en: Business environment means:

options.en: The totality of all individuals, institutions and other forces outside a business that affect its performance
Only the internal rules and policies of a business
The physical surroundings of a factory
Only the customers of a business

explanation.en: Business environment is the sum total of external forces that are beyond the control of a business but affect it.

stem.en: Customers, competitors and suppliers are examples of:

explanation.en: They affect individual firms directly in day-to-day work; general forces (economic, social, political…) affect all firms indirectly.

stem.en: "The demand for a product falls in one region but rises in another for the same change in conditions." This shows that business environment is:

explanation.en: Relativity means the impact of environment differs from country to country and region to region.

stem.en: A rise in health awareness raised the demand for organic food, which led the government to frame food-safety rules. This shows which feature of business environment?

explanation.en: Different parts of the environment (social and legal here) are closely linked with each other.

stem.en: A firm that is the first to spot a new opportunity and act on it gains:

explanation.en: Understanding the environment helps a firm identify opportunities early and gain first mover advantage.

stem.en: An Indian two-wheeler maker noticed that foreign firms were entering the electric scooter market and improved its own models in time. This shows that environment helps to:

options.en: Identify threats and give early warning signals

explanation.en: Environmental awareness warns a firm about threats so that it can prepare in advance.

stem.en: Business is an open system. This means that it:

options.en: Is free from all government control
Gets inputs from the environment and supplies outputs to it

explanation.en: A business takes resources (capital, labour, materials) from the environment and gives back goods and services; this is "tapping useful resources".

stem.en: Which of the following is NOT a point of importance of business environment?

options.en: It helps in planning and policy formulation
It guarantees that the firm will never face losses
It helps in coping with rapid changes

explanation.en: Understanding the environment improves planning and performance but cannot guarantee freedom from losses.

stem.en: Changes in interest rates, inflation and the stock market form part of the:

explanation.en: Interest rates, inflation, incomes and stock market indices are economic conditions.

stem.en: Increasing demand for digital payments because of smartphones and UPI is mainly a change in the:

explanation.en: New scientific and technical innovations such as UPI belong to the technological environment.

stem.en: The requirement of a statutory health warning on cigarette packets is an example of the:

explanation.en: Laws, court rulings and government regulations, such as mandatory warnings, form the legal environment.

stem.en: Growing preference for gym memberships, protein foods and work-from-home among young professionals reflects mainly the:

explanation.en: Customs, lifestyle, values and health consciousness are part of the social environment.

stem.en: The New Economic Policy of India was announced in:

explanation.en: In July 1991 the Government of India announced the New Industrial Policy and economic reforms (LPG).

stem.en: Abolishing industrial licensing in most industries is an example of:

explanation.en: Liberalisation means freeing industry from unnecessary controls such as licensing.

stem.en: Disinvestment of public sector undertakings is a feature of:

explanation.en: Privatisation gives a greater role to the private sector, for example by selling a part of government shares in PSUs.

stem.en: Which of the following was an impact of the LPG policies on Indian business?

options.en: Increased competition and more demanding customers
Larger budgetary support to public sector units

explanation.en: After 1991, competition rose, customers had more choice, technology changed fast, and PSUs lost budgetary support.

stem.en: Demonetisation of ₹500 and ₹1000 notes was announced in India on:

explanation.en: The Government announced on 8 November 2016 that these notes would cease to be legal tender.

stem.en: Demonetisation is viewed as a tax administration measure because:

options.en: It brings unaccounted cash into the open, so it can be taxed

explanation.en: People holding cash had to deposit it in banks, so the government could identify and tax unaccounted income.

stem.en: Which of the following is a feature of demonetisation?

options.en: Increase in the use of black money
A push towards a less-cash, digital economy
Removal of all coins from circulation

explanation.en: Demonetisation aimed to channelise savings into the formal system and promote digital payments (a less-cash economy).

stem.en: Which of these was an aim of demonetisation?

explanation.en: It aimed at curbing black money, corruption, fake currency and terror funding.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Understanding the business environment helps a firm to improve its performance.
Reason (R): Firms that continuously monitor their environment and adopt suitable practices improve their present performance and continue to succeed in the long run.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: Both are true, and R explains how understanding the environment improves performance.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Business environment is the same for all firms in all countries.
Reason (R): The impact of business environment differs from country to country and region to region.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: A is false: environment is relative. R is true: that is exactly why A is false.

stem.en: The preference for baked, low-oil snacks is a change in which dimension of business environment?

explanation.en: Changing tastes and health awareness are social factors.

passage.en: In 2023, a Bengaluru-based snack company, Crunchy Foods, noticed three changes. First, many young customers began to prefer baked and low-oil snacks. Second, the government made it compulsory to print detailed nutrition labels on packets. Third, a new machine became available that bakes snacks using 30% less power. The company changed its product line and packaging within six months.

stem.en: The rule on nutrition labels and the new power-saving machine relate, respectively, to:

explanation.en: A compulsory labelling rule is legal; a new machine is a technological change.

passage.en: In 2023, a Bengaluru-based snack company, Crunchy Foods, noticed three changes. First, many young customers began to prefer baked and low-oil snacks. Second, the government made it compulsory to print detailed nutrition labels on packets. Third, a new machine became available that bakes snacks using 30% less power. The company changed its product line and packaging within six months.

stem.en: Match the following and choose the correct option: (i) Repo rate cut by RBI (ii) Rise in demand for millets (iii) New consumer protection law (iv) Use of AI chatbots by banks — (a) Social (b) Economic (c) Technological (d) Legal.

explanation.en: Repo rate is economic, food preference is social, a law is legal and AI tools are technological.

stem.en: Which of the following statements about business environment are correct? (A) It is dynamic. (B) It is fully controllable by the firm. (C) It involves uncertainty. (D) It is complex.

explanation.en: The environment is dynamic, uncertain and complex, but it is beyond the control of a firm.

stem.en: Which of the following were NOT features or aims of demonetisation?

options.en: Curbing black money and channelising savings into banks
Raising import duties and closing banks
Treating it as a tax administration measure

explanation.en: Demonetisation was about black money, formal savings, digital payments and tax administration, not import duties or bank closures.
